Here is the setup from its README, plus the review pattern it points to. What it does The README calls it a general-purpose Claude Code action for GitHub PRs and issues. It runs on your GitHub runner, and API calls go to the provider you choose: Anthropic direct, Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI or Microsoft Foundry.

articles.title: The 80.52 Short: why a 65B beating a 501B needed a video to be believed
articles.excerpt: I spent last week trying to explain that parameter count stopped being the whole story. A 65B model I run locally scored 80.52 on our eval suite; a 501B frontier model scored lower on the same run. Th…
articles.body: I spent last week trying to explain that parameter count stopped being the whole story. A 65B model I run locally scored 80.52 on our eval suite; a 501B frontier model scored lower on the same run. The number alone sounds like a typo, so I filmed a walkthrough instead of arguing in comments. The Short exists because the gap is real but invisible without seeing the harness. The concrete detail I show on screen: both models got the exact same 200-question multiple-choice set, temperature 0, no system-prompt changes. The only difference was inference path — the 65B ran quantized at Q4_K_M on a single consumer GPU while the 501B ran through its hosted API with defaults. Same questions, same scoring script, and the smaller model won 14 of 20 categories.

articles.title: Running Local LLMs in the Browser with WebGPU and Transformers.js
articles.excerpt: The Evolution of Client-Side Neural Execution By exposing direct access to local GPU compute shaders without the overhead of WebGL hacks, WebGPU allows browsers to execute 4-bit and 8-bit quantized mo…
articles.body: The Evolution of Client-Side Neural Execution For years, executing machine learning models required beefy cloud servers equipped with high-end enterprise GPUs. However, the stabilization of the WebGPU API across major browser engines (Chrome, Edge, Firefox) alongside optimizations in ONNX Runtime Web and Transformers.js has fundamentally transformed this landscape. By exposing direct access to local GPU compute shaders without the overhead of WebGL hacks, WebGPU allows browsers to execute 4-bit and 8-bit quantized models like Qwen 2.5, Phi-3.5, and Llama 3.2 directly inside the client sandbox.

articles.body: Doppelte Zeilen entfernen klingt nach set(rows) . Bei einer echten Kundenliste ist es das selten, denn wenn sich dieselbe Person zweimal anmeldet, entstehen fast nie zwei identische Zeilen. Das Bestelldatum ist ein anderes, die Stadt hat sich geändert, die E-Mail wurde beim zweiten Mal in Großbuchstaben getippt. Ob diese Zeilen als Duplikate zählen, können einem die Daten nicht sagen. Es hängt vom Schlüssel ab, den man vergleicht, und diese Wahl entscheidet alles Weitere: wie viele Zeilen wegfallen, welche bleibt und was dabei verloren geht.

articles.excerpt: AI가 항균 펩타이드(AMP)를 가속할 때, 사람은 어디서 구조를 이해하는가 DeepMind 블로그가 'Accelerating the search for antimicrobial peptides with Google Antigravity'를 공개했습니다. 항생제 내성(AMR) 대응에서 항균 펩타이드(AMP) 탐색 속도를 높이겠다는 내용으로, 후보 서열과 구…
articles.body: AI가 항균 펩타이드(AMP)를 가속할 때, 사람은 어디서 구조를 이해하는가 DeepMind 블로그가 'Accelerating the search for antimicrobial peptides with Google Antigravity'를 공개했습니다. 항생제 내성(AMR) 대응에서 항균 펩타이드(AMP) 탐색 속도를 높이겠다는 내용으로, 후보 서열과 구조를 빠르게 스크리닝하는 파이프라인이 핵심입니다. 여기서 실무자라면 자연스럽게 다음 질문으로 넘어갑니다. 스크리닝된 후보가 실제로 막(membrane)과 어떤 기하학으로 상호작용하는가? 어느 잔기가 결합 포켓을 구성하는가? 이 질문은 서열 스코어로 답이 나오지 않습니다. 결국 3D 좌표를 눈으로 확인해야 합니다. 문제는 '이해'의 병목이다 탐색(discovery) 속도는 AI 덕분에 극적으로 빨라졌지만, 이해(comprehension) 단계는 여전히 2D 스크린에 묶여 있습니다. 회전, 확대, 잔기 간 거리 확인 — 이런 조작을 마우스와 단축키로 반복하는 동안, 입체 감각은 계속 손실됩니다. 이건 단순한 UX 불편이 아니라 파이프라인의 처리량(throughput) 문제입니다. 스크리닝 단계에서 하루에 수백 개 후보를 걸러내도, 각 후보를 검토하는 사람의 인지 대역폭은 그대로입니다. 도구가 빨라질수록 사람 쪽 병목이 상대적으로 더 비싸집니다. 디스크 I/O는 빨라졌는데 CPU가 그대로인 시스템과 비슷합니다.

The work behind it was SEO plus email marketing. But a large part of the SEO half was technical, and it is the part developers control directly. LocalBusiness schema that matches reality The clinic's pages had no structured data tying the business to its services and location. articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission, the first Mars mission in 20 years. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected.

articles.body: We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034.

articles.title: 'I think we will prevail': NASA chief Jared Isaacman on Artemis, China and the new moon race (exclusive)
articles.excerpt: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman during a a Dec. 3, 2025 confirmation hearing. In October of 2026, Isaacman sat down with Space.com to discuss the future of the space agency.
articles.body: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is serious about launching "big rockets" to the moon every single year for the agency's Artemis program. And the new space race with China is fueling that ambition. "I feel good. I feel like we are certainly on a more achievable path to the lunar surface today than where we were before," Isaacman told Space.com. We recently sat down with the NASA chief to discuss the state of the Artemis program , and, off the bat, he made it clear that he's confident in the U.S. space program following the success of April's Artemis II mission around the moon. In fact, just prior to our conversation, it was announced that Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman will become the new deputy director of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory.
